scheme_name: Promoting to Farmer for Post Harvesting & Management (Value Addition)
description:
The Promoting to Farmer for Post Harvesting & Management (Value Addition) scheme is a significant initiative launched by the Government of India. 

This scheme was officially launched in the year 2018. 

It is part of the broader strategy to enhance the income of farmers and improve their livelihoods. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to promote post-harvest management practices among farmers. 

The scheme aims to reduce post-harvest losses which are estimated to be around 20 to 30 percent for various crops. 

By improving post-harvest management, the government seeks to increase the availability of food and enhance food security. 

The scheme also focuses on promoting value addition to agricultural produce. 

This is expected to increase the income of farmers by enabling them to sell their products at higher prices. 

The government has set a target to reduce post-harvest losses by at least 10 percent within the first three years of implementation. 

Farmers participating in the scheme can benefit from various financial assistance programs. 

Under this scheme, farmers can receive up to 50 percent of the cost of equipment and infrastructure for post-harvest management. 

The maximum financial assistance provided can go up to INR 50 lakh per project. 

This financial support is aimed at helping farmers acquire modern technology and equipment. 

The scheme also encourages the establishment of post-harvest management units. 

These units can include facilities for sorting, grading, packaging, and storage of agricultural produce. 

Eligibility for the scheme is primarily focused on farmers and farmer producer organizations. 

Individual farmers must be registered and recognized under the relevant state agricultural departments. 

Farmer producer organizations must have a minimum of 10 members to qualify for the benefits. 

There are no specific age limits set for individual farmers under this scheme. 

However, farmers must demonstrate a commitment to adopting post-harvest management practices. 

Income criteria for eligibility are generally aligned with the definitions provided by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

Farmers must have a documented history of agricultural production to be eligible for assistance. 

The application process for the scheme is straightforward but requires specific documentation. 

Farmers must fill out an application form available at the local agricultural office or online on the official government portal. 

The required documents typically include proof of identity, land ownership documents, and a detailed project proposal. 

Farmers may also need to provide a bank account statement to facilitate the disbursement of funds. 

Once the application is submitted, it undergoes a review process by the local agricultural department. 

The review process usually takes about 30 days from the date of application submission. 

If approved, the financial assistance is disbursed in a phased manner. 

The first installment is typically released upon the approval of the project. 

Subsequent payments are made based on the progress of the project implementation. 

The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

State agricultural departments are responsible for the ground-level execution of the scheme. 

Farmers can contact their local agricultural offices for more information and assistance. 

The scheme also emphasizes training and capacity building for farmers. 

Workshops and training sessions are organized to educate farmers about modern post-harvest techniques. 

These training programs are conducted in collaboration with agricultural universities and research institutions. 

The government aims to train at least 1 million farmers in post-harvest management techniques over the next five years. 

In addition to financial assistance, the scheme also provides access to market linkages. 

Farmers are encouraged to form cooperatives to enhance their bargaining power in the market. 

The scheme has been positively received in various states, with many farmers reporting increased incomes. 

For example, farmers in Punjab have reported a 30 percent increase in income after adopting post-harvest management practices. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 500 crore for the implementation of this scheme over five years. 

Monitoring and evaluation of the scheme are conducted regularly to assess its impact. 

Feedback from farmers is collected to improve the implementation process. 

The scheme is part of the larger initiative to double farmers' income by the year 2022. 

It aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals set by the United Nations, particularly in relation to zero hunger. 

The government is committed to ensuring that farmers have access to the necessary resources and knowledge. 

This scheme is expected to play a crucial role in transforming the agricultural landscape of India. 

By focusing on post-harvest management, the government aims to create a more sustainable and profitable agricultural sector. 

The initiative is also expected to contribute to rural development and job creation. 

Farmers are encouraged to take advantage of this scheme to enhance their productivity and profitability. 

Overall, the Promoting to Farmer for Post Harvesting & Management (Value Addition) scheme represents a significant step towards improving the agricultural economy in India. 

It provides concrete financial support and resources to farmers while promoting sustainable practices. 

The government continues to monitor the progress of the scheme to ensure its effectiveness and reach. 

Farmers are urged to stay informed about the latest updates and opportunities related to this scheme. 

By participating in this initiative, farmers can significantly improve their post-harvest practices and overall economic well-being. 

The scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to uplift the agricultural sector and support farmers across the country.
